main_text.l: Merito suo & satisfactione p̄stita Deo Patri pro peccatis nostris, non tantum doctrina & efficacia, sed etiam persolutione sufficientis λύτρῳ[?] ac pretii redē-tionis pro nobis; ut non tantum intel-ligatur Magister & Doctor noster Chri-stus, qui nobis viam salutis æternæ annuntiarit, & exemplo vitæ & mortis suæ oftenderit ac obsignarit; non tantum intelligatur Dominus & Princeps Vitæ, qui habeat potestatem plenam promittendi & conferendi vitam æternam omnibus verbo suo credentibus & præceptis vitæ obedientibus: sed etiam credatur SPONSOR NOSTER; q; & a nobis sposponderit, & a nobis per-solverit redemtionis nostræ pretium, Salutem promeruerit, se hostiam pro peccatis nostris obtulerit Deo Patri, il-lamq; apud eum valere cupiat pro nostri reconciliatione; ut paulo post hæc manifestis demo-strabitur argumen-tis.

page.notes: The Greek word after "sufficientis" is printed with a small, partly worn ending; the reading λύτρῳ is a best guess. The ornamental asterisks after "argumentis" are printed as "* tis. *" and are copied as the printer set them. The margin note has three lines: "Merito &", "Satisfactio-", and a small ornament; only the first two lines are transcribed. The "p" with a bar in "pstita" is a contraction for "pre" and is written with a macron. The printed "demo-strabitur" may carry a macron over the o; it is written without one.
